items.title: Patient Monitoring (Intraoperative Standards)
items.summary: The 'Monitoring' heading (source_pdf_page 55 in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json, status UNRESOLVED) has NO corresponding node anywhere in toc_inventory.json's 59 chapter-A nodes - unlike the A.S01/A.S06 same-page merges, there was no existing node to split; the TOC-extraction pipeline dropped this heading entirely.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - raw OCR of pdf page 61 (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0061.json) confirms the heading text is 'Canadian Guidelines to the Practice of Anesthesia and Patient Monitoring', immediately followed on the same page by the confirmed body-heading match already recorded for node A.S03 ('Airway Management'). Represented as SU-A-07 with source_node_ids ['UNCATALOGUED:Monitoring@pdf61'] since no real toc_inventory.json node id exists to cite.
items.recommended_action: Coordinator should consider adding a corresponding node to toc_inventory.json for chapter A (between A.S02 and A.S03, pdf page 61) in a future TOC-extraction pass, since this confirms at least one heading is missing from the pipeline's output entirely (not merged, dropped) - the same class of gap that produced the ELOM reference-disclaimer reattribution case. Flagged informational/low-priority since chapter A's own crosswalk is unaffected (SU-A-07 is fully resolved and validated).

items.title: Malignant Hyperthermia
items.summary: No MCC objective names malignant hyperthermia verbatim, despite it being one of the highest-yield, most classically board-tested facts in anesthesia. The best available anchor, 107-1 'Fever and hyperthermia' (MODERATE strength), only lists the mechanistically-analogous 'drug-induced syndromes (e.g., neuroleptic malignant syndrome, serotonin syndrome)' in its causal_conditions, not MH itself. This is honestly documented in the crosswalk's mapping_rationale rather than forced to a false STRONG match.
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter A's own crosswalk (evidence is defensible at MODERATE); flagged for coordinator awareness in case future MCC objectives_registry.json updates add MH explicitly, or in case other chapters (e.g. Pediatrics, Surgery) encounter the same naming gap and a cross-chapter registry annotation would help.

items.title: References/Landmark-Trials merge pattern confirmed genuine (contrast with ELOM)
items.summary: CP.S06's merged_duplicate_headings field lists 'References' alongside 'Landmark Pharmacology Trials' (both indexed to TOC page CP14 / pdf 188), structurally identical in shape to the ELOM ELOM.S04 case where a 'References'-labelled node turned out to be a misattributed disclaimer paragraph rather than a genuine bibliography.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - raw OCR of body page 0188.json (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0188.json) confirms CP.S06's 'References' heading here genuinely IS a correctly-attributed, >30-entry chapter bibliography (author/journal/year citations throughout: e.g. Boyer, 'The serotonin syndrome', NEJM 2005; Busse et al., opioid-therapy guideline, CMAJ 2017), with no clinical/testable prose mixed in. No content was reattached elsewhere. Represented as SU-CP-19 (Landmark Pharmacology Trials) + SU-CP-20 (References/Bibliography), both REFERENCE_ONLY.
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter CP's own crosswalk. Flagged for coordinator awareness that the same_page_toc_merge_protocol.md 'References' detection signal (step to check whether a References node is genuine or a misattribution) produces DIFFERENT outcomes across chapters - genuine in Chapter CP, misattributed in Chapter ELOM - confirming the protocol's per-chapter case-by-case verification requirement is doing real work and should not be shortcut in future chapters that show this same merge shape.

items.title: Opioid Therapy nested under Autonomic Physiology heading despite thematic mismatch
items.summary: CP.S04's same-page merge nests 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain' as a third printed TOC sub-bullet under 'Autonomic Physiology & Pharmacology' (alongside Parasympathetic/Sympathetic Nervous System), even though opioid-prescribing guideline content has no thematic connection to autonomic nervous system physiology.
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - raw OCR of body pages 0185.json/0186.json confirms 'Opioid Therapy and Chronic Non-Cancer Pain' is its own genuine, independently-bolded body heading, printed immediately after the Autonomic Physiology content ends (Table 3 / Figure 8) with no textual continuity between the two. Represented as its own separate study unit, SU-CP-16, rather than folded into SU-CP-15 (Autonomic Nervous System Physiology and Pharmacology).
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter CP's own crosswalk. Flagged for coordinator awareness that Toronto Notes' own printed TOC layout occasionally nests a thematically-unrelated heading under a preceding section purely for column-space/typesetting reasons rather than genuine hierarchy - study-unit derivation should continue to prioritize confirmed body-heading structure and thematic coherence over raw TOC indentation, consistent with existing protocol guidance.

items.title: No dedicated MCC 'clinical pharmacology principles' objective
items.summary: 16 of this chapter's 20 study units (13 of 17 total OBJECTIVE_REFERENCE citations) anchor on the single MCC objective 125 'Prescribing practices', because it is the only Medical Expert objective dedicated to safe/individualized prescribing broadly. However, 125's own enabling-objectives text does not name specific PK/PD mechanisms (bioavailability, volume of distribution, half-life, CYP-mediated metabolism, receptor agonism/antagonism, therapeutic index) verbatim - the mapping_rationale on each affected unit (e.g. SU-CP-04 through SU-CP-11) honestly documents this as a MODERATE-strength inference from 125's broader risk-benefit/comorbidity/genetics language rather than a verbatim match.
items.resolution_status: No action required for chapter CP's own crosswalk - every affected unit still achieves at least MODERATE mapping_strength with a defensible textual anchor (0 WEAK mappings in this chapter).
items.recommended_action: Flagged for coordinator awareness in case future MCC objectives_registry.json updates add a more granular pharmacology-principles objective, or in case other chapters (e.g., Medicine's own therapeutics content, Psychiatry's psychopharmacology sections) encounter the same single-objective concentration and a cross-chapter registry annotation would help distribute evidence more precisely.

items.title: 9 real Dermatology headings have no toc_inventory.json node at all (dropped, not merged)
items.summary: Chapter D's TOC page (pdf 189) is a two-column layout whose OCR interleaved adjacent-column text. 7 headings are recorded UNRESOLVED in research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json (Introduction to Skin, Morphology, Patterns and Distribution, Differential Diagnoses for Common Presentations, Common Skin Lesions, Acneiform Eruptions, Papulosquamous Diseases); 2 further headings with real body content (Pre-Malignant Skin Conditions, Dermatologic Therapies) have no unresolved_headings.json entry either - they were silently dropped by the extraction pass rather than flagged. This is the same class of gap chapter A's 'Monitoring' heading exhibited (see review_queue.json's existing SU-A-07 entry).
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED (not left open) - all 9 were located via body-heading confirmation (raw OCR + derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/ normalized text, pdf 190-246) and assigned synthetic UNCATALOGUED:D-* source_node_ids per the documented convention. 2 of the 9 (Common Skin Lesions, Acneiform Eruptions) needed no standalone unit because their child subsections are already accounted for via existing merged nodes. The remaining 7 are represented as SU-D-02, SU-D-03, SU-D-13, SU-D-14, SU-D-34, SU-D-45, SU-D-46, and folded into SU-D-48 (Landmark Trials). See study_units.json's unresolved_heading_resolution field for the complete per-heading resolution.
items.recommended_action: Coordinator should consider adding corresponding nodes to toc_inventory.json for chapter D in a future TOC-extraction pass (Introduction to Skin at pdf 190-192; Morphology/Patterns/DDx at pdf 192-196; Pre-Malignant Skin Conditions at pdf 227; Papulosquamous Diseases at pdf 208-211; Sunscreens and Preventative Therapy at pdf 240; Dermatologic Therapies at pdf 241-242; Landmark Dermatology Trials at pdf 244-245), since this confirms the extraction pipeline can silently drop headings entirely (not just merge them) on a badly-OCR'd two-column TOC page. Flagged informational/low-priority since chapter D's own crosswalk is unaffected (all 9 are fully resolved and validated).

items.title: Unusually high rate of two-column TOC node-title merges (~20 of 42 nodes)
items.summary: Beyond the 9 fully-dropped headings above, roughly 20 of chapter D's 42 toc_inventory.json nodes carry titles that concatenate two real, physically distant headings that happened to share a TOC line during OCR (e.g. D.S06's title 'Cysts Malignant Skin Tumours' merges a pdf-196 subsection with a pdf-228 major heading 32 pages away). This is a substantially higher merge rate than any previously completed chapter (C, ELOM, A, CP).
items.resolution_status: INDEPENDENTLY RESOLVED for all 20 nodes - each was split into its constituent real fragments via body-heading confirmation, with the full per-node ledger recorded in study_units.json's same_page_merge_resolutions field. No mapping-quality impact: source_accounting passed with 0 unaccounted nodes and 0 WEAK mcc_evidence citations resulted.
items.recommended_action: No action required for chapter D itself (fully resolved). Flagged informational so the coordinator is aware that chapter D's toc_inventory.json node titles are less reliable as literal section titles than other chapters if they are ever consumed directly (e.g. by tooling) rather than through study_units.json's resolved titles.
